```{r setup, include=FALSE}

invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
# R code here is ASCII only (HTML entities for special characters), so the page renders the same in any locale
A <- "docs/assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum"
tq <- fread(file.path(A, "tissue_qtls.tsv")); st <- fread(file.path(A, "isoform_steps.tsv"))
pa <- fread(file.path(A, "params.tsv")); g <- fread(file.path(A, "gene_pips.tsv")); cv <- fread(file.path(A, "convergence.tsv"))
RUNS <- c(es="eQTL + sQTL", esi="eQTL + sQTL + irQTL", i="irQTL only")
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
fp <- function(x) vapply(x, function(z) if (is.na(z)) "NA" else format(signif(z, 2)), "")
cell <- function(x) fifelse(is.na(x), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", x))
iso <- pa[run == "esi" & type == "irQTL"]
cb <- tq[tissue == "Brain_Cerebellum"]
g8 <- function(r) g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]
gene_table <- function(d) paste(knitr::kable(d[order(-combined_pip), .(gene_name, combined_pip=sprintf("%.2f", combined_pip), eQTL_pip=cell(eQTL_pip),
  sQTL_pip=cell(sQTL_pip), irQTL_pip=cell(irQTL_pip), Traits=n_traits, `Top trait`=top_trait, `Top trait type`=top_type,
  `susie_pip (top trait)`=sprintf("%.2f", top_trait_pip), z=sprintf("%.1f", z))], escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrrllrr"), collapse="\n")
```

# How we selected the tissue

We chose the brain tissue with the most isoform-ratio QTLs (irQTLs: QTLs for an
isoform's share of its gene's expression), since SCZ is a brain
trait. The counts are Pantry's conditionally independent cis-QTLs per GTEx v8
tissue (`gtex.separate_kdp.qtls.tsv.gz`, downloaded 2026-10-29).

```{r tissues}
d <- tq[brain == TRUE | rank <= 3][order(rank)]
knitr::kable(d[, .(Rank=rank, Tissue=gsub("_", " ", tissue), `Pantry code`=code, `irQTLs`=fmt(isoform_qtls),
  Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(isoform_genes), eQTLs=fmt(eqtls), `Splicing QTLs`=fmt(sqtls))], align="rllrrrrr")
```

- **Rank:** among all `r nrow(tq)` tissues, by the number of irQTLs. The
  table shows the top three tissues overall and every brain tissue.
- **irQTLs:** independent cis-QTLs; **Isoforms** and **Genes** are the
  isoforms and genes they belong to. **eQTLs** and **Splicing QTLs** are Pantry's
  expression and intron-excision QTLs in the same tissue, for comparison.

Brain Cerebellum has the most among brain tissues: `r fmt(cb$isoform_qtls)`
irQTLs in `r fmt(cb$isoforms)` isoforms of `r fmt(cb$isoform_genes)` genes.
Testis has the most overall. Pantry codes the two cerebellum tissues BRNCHA and
BRNCHB. Its covariate files have 209 samples for BRNCHA and 175 for BRNCHB, the
GTEx v8 sample sizes of Brain Cerebellum and Cerebellar Hemisphere, so BRNCHA is
Brain Cerebellum.

# How the runs were set up

- **GWAS:** PGC schizophrenia, `ieu-b-5102` (N = 127,906), z-scores harmonized to
  the UK Biobank (UKB) LD reference, as for the M-cTWAS paper.
- **eQTL and sQTL weights:** the paper's GTEx v8 PredictDB expression and splicing
  models for Brain Cerebellum.
- **irQTL weights** (our definition): one trait per isoform, from Pantry's
  independent cis-QTLs in Brain Cerebellum. They come from the genes significant
  in Pantry's permutation test, q < 0.05.
  - Each isoform's QTL is its strongest independent variant (smallest nominal p)
    among single-base variants in the UKB reference that are not
    strand-ambiguous.
  - The weight is that variant's effect on the isoform ratio (tensorQTL's
    slope); with one SNP per trait, only its sign matters.
  - Genes come from Pantry's own annotation. We used top QTLs, not Munro's
    prediction models.
- **Settings, as the paper's runs:** each QTL type is its own group, with protein-coding genes only and LD
  from the UKB reference. eQTL and sQTL weights are scaled (`scale_predictdb_weights`), the
  isoform weights are not (one SNP per trait). No thinning, one prior variance shared
  by all groups (`shared_all`), up to 5 signals per region (L = 5).
- **Three runs:** eQTL + sQTL (the paper's QTL types), eQTL + sQTL + irQTL,
  and irQTL only (added 2026-11-03, to test whether the irQTLs
  carry signal on their own). All use the same settings.
- **Not done yet:** merging regions and checking LD mismatch.

```{r steps}
knitr::kable(st[, .(Step=step, QTLs=fmt(qtls), Isoforms=fmt(isoforms), Genes=fmt(genes))], align="lrrr")
```

The irQTL weights at each step. The last row is the weights. cTWAS then
keeps the isoforms of protein-coding genes whose QTL is in the GWAS:
`r fmt(iso$group_size)` traits.

## What the tables and figures show

**Parameters**, the output of `summarize_param()`:

- **group_size:** molecular traits that reach cTWAS after matching to the GWAS and the LD reference.
- **group_prior:** the estimated prior probability that a trait (or a SNP) is causal.
- **group_prior_var:** the prior variance of a causal effect, shared by all groups (`shared_all`).
- **log_enrichment:** the log of a group's prior over the SNP prior, with its
  standard error; **enrichment_pval** is its p-value.
- **group_pve:** the proportion of SCZ variance explained by the group;
  **total_pve** sums all groups and SNPs.
- **prop_heritability:** a group's `group_pve` over `total_pve`, the slices of the
  pie charts.

**Convergence**, from `make_convergence_plots()`: the estimates at each iteration
of the parameter estimation (proportion causal &pi; is `group_prior`, effect size
&sigma;<sup>2</sup> is `group_prior_var`, enrichment is
&pi;<sub>G</sub>/&pi;<sub>S</sub>, and PVE).

**Gene-level PIPs:** `combined_pip` combines all of a gene's molecular traits and
QTL types with `combine_gene_pips()` (`by = "type"`, `method = "combine_cs"`,
`filter_cs = FALSE`). **eQTL_pip**, **sQTL_pip** and **irQTL_pip** are the gene's
PIP from each QTL type; "&ndash;" means the gene has no trait of that type in a
fine-mapped region. The mapping table assigns each trait to its gene: the paper's
PredictDB mapping for eQTL genes and sQTL introns, and Pantry's annotation for
isoforms.

# Results

## Parameters

```{r params}
w <- merge(pa[type != "SNP"], pa[type == "SNP", .(run, snp_prior=group_prior)], by="run")[order(match(run, names(RUNS)), match(type, c("eQTL", "sQTL", "irQTL")))]
knitr::kable(w[, .(Run=RUNS[run], group, group_size=fmt(group_size), group_prior=sprintf("%.5f", group_prior), `group_prior (SNP)`=sprintf("%.5f", snp_prior),
  group_prior_var=sprintf("%.1f", group_prior_var), `log_enrichment (log_enrichment_se)`=sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", log_enrichment, log_enrichment_se),
  enrichment_pval=fp(enrichment_pval), group_pve=sprintf("%.4f", group_pve), total_pve=sprintf("%.3f", total_pve),
  prop_heritability=sprintf("%.5f", prop_heritability))], align="llrrrrrrrrr")
```

## Convergence {.tabset}

`r sprintf("%s converged in %d iterations. %s stopped at %d iterations without converging: the irQTL prior was still decreasing towards zero while the eQTL, sQTL and SNP estimates had settled, so its estimate is an upper bound.", RUNS[["es"]], cv[run == "es", iterations], RUNS[["esi"]], cv[run == "esi", iterations])`
Both fine-mapped `r fmt(cv[run == "es", regions])` regions. `r sprintf("%s %s in %d iterations and fine-mapped %s regions.", RUNS[["i"]], if (cv[run == "i", converged]) "converged" else "did not converge", cv[run == "i", iterations], fmt(cv[run == "i", regions]))`

```{r conv, results="asis"}
for (r in names(RUNS)) {
  cat("### ", RUNS[[r]], "\n\n", sep="")
  cat("![](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/convergence_", r, ".png)\n\n[Open as PDF](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/convergence_", r, ".pdf)\n\n", sep="")
}
```

## Gene-level PIPs

### Genes with combined_pip of at least 0.8 in any run

```{r overview}
gn <- sort(unique(g[combined_pip >= 0.8, gene_name]))
pick <- function(r, col) vapply(gn, function(x) { v <- g[run == r & gene_name == x][[col]]; if (length(v)) v[1] else NA_real_ }, 0)
o <- data.table(gene_name=gn, a=pick("es", "combined_pip"), b=pick("esi", "combined_pip"), e=pick("esi", "eQTL_pip"), s=pick("esi", "sQTL_pip"), i=pick("esi", "irQTL_pip"),
                c=pick("i", "combined_pip"))[order(-b)]
knitr::kable(o[, .(gene_name, `combined_pip (eQTL + sQTL)`=cell(a), `combined_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(b),
  `eQTL_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(e), `sQTL_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(s), `irQTL_pip (+ irQTL)`=cell(i),
  `combined_pip (irQTL only)`=cell(c))], escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrrr")
```

Columns 4&ndash;6 split the second run's `combined_pip` by QTL type. The last
column is the irQTL-only run; "&ndash;" means the gene was not in a
fine-mapped region there.

### By run {.tabset}

Genes with `combined_pip` of at least 0.5.

```{r gene_tabs, results="asis"}
for (r in names(RUNS)) {
  cat("#### ", RUNS[[r]], "\n\n", sep="")
  cat(gene_table(g[run == r & combined_pip >= 0.5]), "\n\n", sep="")
}
```

- **Traits:** the gene's molecular traits in fine-mapped regions, over all QTL types.
- **Top trait:** the trait with the largest `susie_pip`: its ID (an eQTL gene, an
  sQTL intron or an isoform), type, `susie_pip` and z-score (z).

## All genes

```{r all_genes}
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(g[, .(Run=RUNS[run], gene_name, combined_pip=round(combined_pip, 3), eQTL_pip=round(eQTL_pip, 3), sQTL_pip=round(sQTL_pip, 3),
  irQTL_pip=round(irQTL_pip, 3), Traits=n_traits, `Top trait`=top_trait, `Top trait type`=top_type, `susie_pip (top trait)`=round(top_trait_pip, 3),
  z=round(z, 2))][order(-combined_pip)]), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", extensions="Buttons",
  options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE, dom="Bfrtip", buttons=c("copy", "csv")), caption="Every gene in a fine-mapped region, in every run.")
```

**Code:** `long_read_RNA/15.ctwas_gtex_isoform/`:

- `0.build_isoform_topqtl.R`: the irQTL top-QTL weights and their mapping table.
- `1.run_ctwas.R` and `.sbatch`: the three runs (QTL types `es`, `esi` and `i`).
- `2.summarize.R`: this page's tables and figures.

**Downloads:** [tissue counts](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/tissue_qtls.tsv),
[parameters](assets/ctwas_gtex_SCZ_Brain_Cerebellum/params.tsv),
